newsitem.title: pakistan: Pakistan arrests six executives for alleged fraud.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan arrests six executives for alleged fraud.

text.p: Pakistani authorities have arrested six executives of a company said to have links with the jailed husband of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, according to a government statement obtained on Wednesday.
It said the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) had seized the six men in Karachi on Tuesday in raids designed to foil what it said was a plan to move company records to Dubai.
Among the six men named are executives of the Karachi-based Schon Group and its National Fibres Ltd subsidiary. One was arrested at his residence.

Records seized from the house reveal "astonishing and startling information, including details of visits abroad of the first couple (Bhutto and her husband Asif Ali Zardari) and the mysterious activities of Mr Zardari," the statement said.
Zardari, investment minister in his wife's government, has been in jail since President Farooq Leghari sacked Bhutto on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
The statement said one charge against Schon Group alleged that its management had caused a loss of more than 183 million rupees ($45 million) to state-owned Habib Bank Limited.

It also cited financial irregularities in the group's 1992 acquisition of the previously state-owned National Fibres Ltd from the Privatisation Commission, saying Schon had still not paid 400 million rupees of the purchase price of 760 million.
It said Zardari had helped Schon Group obtain a 200 million rupee equity participation from State Life Insurance, Allied Bank of Pakistan and the National Investment Trust.
The statement listed several other alleged frauds by by the accused, none of whom could be reached for comment.

Schon Bank Ltd, which is mostly owned by the Schon Group, said in a statement on Wednesday that none of the detainees was employed by the bank and that the FIA investigations had nothing to do with Schon Bank Ltd or any of its employees.

"There are no big withdrawals, the bank is meeting its commitments and there is no problem with the bank," Schon Bank's general manager, S.M. Husaini, told Reuters when asked about stock market rumours of a run on the bank.
